subject: Post-demo: TTFT & streaming cadence requirements + pilot next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@shoply.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.n@shoply.com
Date: 2026-08-27T15:12:00-04:00
Subject: Follow-up: TTFT targets and streaming cadence (Shoply use-case)

Hi Rafael —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick write-up from our side to make sure we're aligned on performance needs before the pilot: 

- Primary flow: web chat widget for customer support (short prompts, multi-turn).
- TTFT target: median <= 250 ms for first token, p95 <= 450 ms.
- Typical request size: ~30-120 tokens prompt (user + context), expected response 50-200 tokens.
- Concurrency: sustained ~120 concurrent chat sessions during peak; peak bursts up to ~220 concurrent sessions for short windows (~5-10m).
- Throughput: target ~700 qps at peak (counting concurrent sessions * expected message frequency).
- Streaming: we need streaming responses to show tokens asap. Prefer SSE but OK with WebSocket; important is chunk cadence of ~80-200 ms between emitted chunks (i.e., low-latency partial updates).
- Cold-start tolerance: acceptable for rare infra events but prefer warm pools to avoid >2s TTFT spikes.

Priya and I want a short pilot that validates TTFT and chunk cadence with our sample prompt set. Can Redwood run a 48-hour pilot against a hosted/stage endpoint and provide per-route latency/cadence metrics?

Also attaching a short sample prompt file (shoply_prompt_samples.csv).

Thanks,
Jordan Lee
Head of Conversational Products
Shoply

Attachments: shoply_prompt_samples.csv (csv, 12KB)

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Follow-up: TTFT targets and streaming cadence (Shoply use-case)

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear targets and sample prompts. Recapping and proposing next steps so we have an actionable pilot plan: 

Recap of requirements (we heard):
- Median TTFT <= 250 ms, p95 <= 450 ms for first token on web chat
- Sustained concurrency ~120, spikes to ~220
- Streaming with 80–200 ms chunk cadence (SSE preferred; WS acceptable)
- Sample prompt set provided (thanks)

Proposed pilot (48–72 hours):
1) Environment: we'll provision a dedicated pilot pool (hosted but isolated) sized to approximate your peak concurrency.
2) Baseline run: synthetic replay of your prompt set to validate TTFT and chunk cadence. We'll run both warm and cold-start tests.
3) Instrumentation: we will expose per-request traces and per-route dashboards showing TTFT (first-byte vs. first-token), per-chunk delta times, token throughput, and GPU utilization.
4) Acceptance criteria: median TTFT <= 250 ms and chunk cadence 80–200 ms for >= 90% of streaming responses during sustained load.
5) Deliverables: raw traces, aggregated SLO report (median/p95/p99), and configuration recommendations (batching, prefix cache, quantization profile).

Technical ask from your side before kickoff:
- Confirm which streaming transport you want us to use for the pilot (SSE or WebSocket).
- Provide a small set (50–100) of representative sessions with expected context length distribution (if any sessions require long context, flag them).
- Any IP allowlist or network constraints so we can provision access.

I'll loop in Karthik (infra) and Marissa (CS) to outline the test harness and customer success milestones. If you're available, we can kick off the pilot Monday morning (Aug 31).

Next steps: Jordan to confirm transport and send the session distribution; Redwood to send a short pilot runbook and cost estimate.

Best,

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Follow-up: TTFT targets and streaming cadence (Shoply use-case)

Adding a few technical notes to make the pilot measurements reliable: 

1) TTFT measurement: we distinguish between HTTP first byte (network/TCP handshake + TLS) and token emission time. For SLOs we will report first-token time measured at the server-side emission time and observed client-side delta when possible. Please note p95 will be sensitive to cold starts and KV-cache miss rates.

2) Warm pools: to meet median <= 250 ms we will keep a small warm pool. If you expect many infrequent sessions (low QPS per session) that causes caching inefficiencies, share that distribution.

3) Chunk cadence knobs: chunk cadence isn't only runtime-driven; model tokenizer and response generation patterns affect it. We can enforce a minimum chunk flush policy (e.g., flush partial buffers every X ms or every Y tokens). For your 80–200 ms target, plan to test both time-based flush (flush every 100ms) and token-threshold flush (e.g., every 8 tokens) so we can see which is more stable.

4) Quantization/Perf tradeoffs: some quantization profiles improve throughput but increase per-token latency slightly. We'll include two configurations in the pilot: (A) latency-first (no aggressive quant), (B) cost-first (int8-ish quant profile) so you can see delta.

5) Synthetic load: we'll run a Poisson arrival process for steady-state and a short-burst runner for the spike scenarios. We'll provide the harness and an endpoint to start the test.

I'll attach our internal SLO measurement checklist for reproducibility. Small ask for Shoply: share any client-side logging you can (first-byte observed timestamp) to correlate with server traces.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-measurement-guidelines.txt
